page: Compress Middleware for automatic response body compression based on Accept-Encoding header. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {compress} from 'hono/compress'. Also exports COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX for custom filters. Compression schemes: gzip, deflate. HTTP headers: Accept-Encoding (request), Content-Type (response). Options: encoding ('gzip' | 'deflate', both allowed by default, gzip prioritized if both in Accept-Encoding), threshold (number bytes, default 1024), contentTypeFilter (RegExp | function, default COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX). Important note: Not needed on Cloudflare Workers or Deno Deploy (automatic compression). RegExp example: /^application\/json/ compresses only JSON. Function example: (type) => COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX.test(type) || type === 'application/x-myformat' extends default. Custom content-type: application/x-myformat pattern. Minimum compression size: 1024 bytes threshold. Questions: How to compress responses? Which schemes are supported? When not to use this middleware? How to compress only specific content types? What's the size threshold? Can I customize compression? What's the default behavior?

Compress middleware basic usage. app.use(compress()). Applies compression to responses based on Accept-Encoding header. Automatic scheme selection. Minimal configuration. Questions: How to enable compression? What's the simplest usage? Does it need configuration?

Compress middleware options specification. Optional: encoding ('gzip' | 'deflate', both allowed if not specified, gzip prioritized if both in Accept-Encoding header, restricts to single scheme if specified). Optional: threshold (number in bytes, default 1024, minimum size to compress). Optional: contentTypeFilter (RegExp | (contentType: string) => boolean, default uses COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX for built-in list). RegExp example: /^application\/json/ compresses JSON only. Function example: (type) => COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX.test(type) || type === 'application/x-myformat' extends defaults. Exported regex for composition. Note: Cloudflare Workers and Deno Deploy automatically compress responses, making this middleware unnecessary on those platforms. Middleware primarily useful for Node.js, Bun, and other runtimes without automatic compression. Platform-specific: Cloudflare Workers auto-compresses, Deno Deploy auto-compresses, other runtimes need explicit middleware. Questions: Do I need this on Cloudflare Workers?
